claim: Growth plate cartilage is comprised of three major growth zones along its proximodistal axis: resting (RZ), proliferative (PZ), and hypertrophic (HZ).
source: The tissue is comprised of three major growth zones along its proximodistal axis: resting (RZ), proliferative (PZ), and hypertrophic (HZ).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1a showing the schematic diagram of growth plate cartilage structure.

claim: Progenitor resting chondrocytes are spherical and dispersed.
source: The progenitor resting chondrocytes are spherical and dispersed whereas proliferative cells are ellipsoidal and more regularly arranged.
evidence: This is directly stated in the figure caption describing the characteristics of resting zone cells.

claim: Proliferative cells are ellipsoidal and more regularly arranged.
source: The progenitor resting chondrocytes are spherical and dispersed whereas proliferative cells are ellipsoidal and more regularly arranged.
evidence: This is directly stated in the figure caption describing the characteristics of proliferative zone cells.

claim: Hypertrophic cells are enlarged and terminally differentiated.
source: The enlarged hypertrophic cells are terminally differentiated and are subsequently replaced by osteoblasts.
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption describing hypertrophic zone characteristics.

claim: Hypertrophic cells are subsequently replaced by osteoblasts.
source: The enlarged hypertrophic cells are terminally differentiated and are subsequently replaced by osteoblasts.
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption and is consistent with established knowledge of endochondral ossification.

claim: A simple model to explain column formation involves oriented division orthogonal to the proximodistal axis followed by cell rearrangement.
source: A simple model to explain column formation of proliferative cells involves oriented division orthogonal to the proximodistal axis followed by cell rearrangement.
evidence: This model is explicitly stated in the figure caption and illustrated in Figure 1b.

claim: Multicolor clonal analysis using RIA retroviruses can distinguish individual clones by distinct fluorescent colors.
source: A mixture of recombinant replication-incompetent avian (RIA) retrovirus with distinct fluorescent markers is injected into chicken limb buds.
evidence: The methodology is described in the text and illustrated in Figure 1c showing the principle of viral-based multicolor clonal analysis.

claim: If the simple model is correct, only single columns with distinct and uniform monocolor should be visualized in cartilage.
source: If the simple model is correct, only single columns with distinct and uniform monocolor should be visualized in cartilage.
evidence: This is a prediction stated in the figure caption based on the simple model hypothesis.

claim: Resting zone clones displayed radial expansion with arbitrary growth direction.
source: While the growth direction of resting clones was arbitrary (d) (n = 30), proliferative clones were arranged in either single or multi-columns that appeared to be mainly in the growth direction (f1, f2) (n = 46).
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption and supported by data from n=30 clones shown in Figure 1d.

claim: Proliferative clones were arranged in either single or multi-columns mainly in the growth direction.
source: While the growth direction of resting clones was arbitrary (d) (n = 30), proliferative clones were arranged in either single or multi-columns that appeared to be mainly in the growth direction (f1, f2) (n = 46).
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption and supported by data from n=46 clones shown in Figure 1f.

claim: Some multi-columns were intermingled with neighboring clones.
source: Some multi-columns were intermingled with neighboring clones (white arrow, f1).
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption and indicated by a white arrow in Figure 1f1.

claim: The mean angle between the minor axis of proliferative cells and the tissue proximodistal axis was 12°.
source: The mean Φ in the proliferative and resting regions was 12° and 42°, respectively.
evidence: This quantitative measurement is stated in the figure caption and shown in Figure 1h.

claim: The mean angle between the minor axis of resting cells and the tissue proximodistal axis was 42°.
source: The mean Φ in the proliferative and resting regions was 12° and 42°, respectively.
evidence: This quantitative measurement is stated in the figure caption and shown in Figure 1h.

claim: The standard deviation of cell orientation in the proliferative zone was 3°.
source: The standard deviation (SD) of Φ in the proliferative zone was 3° (h2) (n = 18), smaller than cell orientation (12°), demonstrating these cells stacked in rows.
evidence: This quantitative measurement is stated in the figure caption based on n=18 measurements shown in Figure 1h2.

claim: The small standard deviation of cell orientation (3°) compared to mean cell orientation (12°) demonstrates that proliferative cells stack in rows.
source: The standard deviation (SD) of Φ in the proliferative zone was 3° (h2) (n = 18), smaller than cell orientation (12°), demonstrating these cells stacked in rows.
evidence: This interpretation is explicitly stated in the figure caption based on the quantitative data.

claim: Single columns have a standard deviation of θ lower than 12°.
source: Using 12° as a threshold, if the SD of θ was lower than this value, the column was grouped as a single column (n = 29); otherwise, we called it complex one (n = 20) (i2).
evidence: This classification criterion is stated in the figure caption and applied to n=29 single columns shown in Figure 1i.

claim: Complex columns have a standard deviation of θ higher than 12°.
source: Using 12° as a threshold, if the SD of θ was lower than this value, the column was grouped as a single column (n = 29); otherwise, we called it complex one (n = 20) (i2).
evidence: This classification criterion is stated in the figure caption and applied to n=20 complex columns shown in Figure 1i.

claim: Most single columns were generally parallel to the growth direction with mean orientation of 11.77°.
source: While most single columns were generally parallel to the growth direction (mean orientation was 11.77°) (n = 21), multi-columns were slightly shifted with higher variations (mean orientation was 22.82°) (n = 21) (j2).
evidence: This quantitative measurement is stated in the figure caption based on n=21 single columns shown in Figure 1j.

claim: Multi-columns were slightly shifted with higher variations and mean orientation of 22.82°.
source: While most single columns were generally parallel to the growth direction (mean orientation was 11.77°) (n = 21), multi-columns were slightly shifted with higher variations (mean orientation was 22.82°) (n = 21) (j2).
evidence: This quantitative measurement is stated in the figure caption based on n=21 multi-columns shown in Figure 1j.

claim: Proliferative cells were generally parallel to the proximodistal axis with average Φ of about 12°.
source: While the proliferative cells were generally parallel to the proximodistal axis (Average Φ was about 12°) (n = 20), the orientations of resting cells were arbitrary (Average Φ was about 43°, with larger standard deviation) (n = 28).
evidence: This measurement is stated in the figure supplement caption based on n=20 cells shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The orientations of resting cells were arbitrary with average Φ of about 43° and larger standard deviation.
source: While the proliferative cells were generally parallel to the proximodistal axis (Average Φ was about 12°) (n = 20), the orientations of resting cells were arbitrary (Average Φ was about 43°, with larger standard deviation) (n = 28).
evidence: This measurement is stated in the figure supplement caption based on n=28 cells shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Sister cells remained connected to each other after cytokinesis.
source: Sister cells appeared to be positioned orthogonal to the tissue proximodistal axis and physically coupled after cytokinesis.
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption and shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Sister cells remained in contact 10 hr after cytokinesis.
source: This method confirmed sister cells remained in contact 10 hr after cytokinesis (n = 5) (c).
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption based on quantitative analysis of n=5 cell pairs shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Most sister cell pairs (7/8) underwent pivot from lateral alignment into single columns along the proximodistal axis.
source: Most pairs (7/8) were initially aligned lateral to each other (low ω at time 0) and then underwent pivot (progressive increase of ω) into a single column (ω was between 70–100°) along the tissue proximodistal axis (n = 8).
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption based on analysis of n=8 cell pairs shown in Figure 2g.

claim: One sister cell pair underwent only partial pivot of about 50°.
source: Noticeably, one pair underwent partial pivot for about 50° only (red line).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption and shown as a red line in Figure 2g.

claim: Cell pivot behavior produces single columns whereas intercalation refines multi-columns.
source: Schematic diagrams showing how distinct types of cell rearrangements generating corresponding columns: cell pivot behavior produces single columns whereas intercalation refines multi-columns.
evidence: This model is explicitly stated in the figure caption and illustrated in Figure 2h.

claim: Chondrocytes undergo oriented divisions orthogonal to the proximodistal axis.
source: The results showed orthogonal division to proximodistal axis (n = 32).
evidence: This is stated in the figure supplement caption based on n=32 dividing cells shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Partial intercalation was observed inside GFP clones.
source: In the chick metacarpals clonally labeled with distinct fluorophores via RIA infection, partial intercalation was observed inside one GFP (green) clone (white arrows) (n = 8) (a), and between mCherry (red) and CFP (blue) clones (white arrows) (n = 2) (b).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure supplement caption based on n=8 clones shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2a.

claim: Partial intercalation was observed between mCherry and CFP clones.
source: In the chick metacarpals clonally labeled with distinct fluorophores via RIA infection, partial intercalation was observed inside one GFP (green) clone (white arrows) (n = 8) (a), and between mCherry (red) and CFP (blue) clones (white arrows) (n = 2) (b).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure supplement caption based on n=2 instances shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2b.

claim: Fzd7-ΔPDB expression disrupts normal chondrocyte cell polarity in developing chick cartilage.
source: To this end, we took advantage of a truncated version of Frizzled-7 (Fzd7) lacking the PDZ binding domain (Fzd7-ΔPDB) that functions as a dominant-negative mutant (Kuss et al., 2014) and disrupts normal chondrocyte cell polarity in developing chick cartilage (Li and Dudley, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to previous work (Kuss et al., 2014) and (Li and Dudley, 2009).

claim: Fzd7-ΔPDB expressing cells became rounder and disorganized.
source: By co-infecting A coated virus (RCASA) harboring the Fzd7-ΔPDB mutant together with RCASB-H2B-GFP-2A-mCherry into chicken limbs, we achieved super-infection, such that many fluorescently labeled cells became rounder and disorganized (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) undergoing cell division in arbitrary directions rather than along the mediolateral axis (Figure 3a) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) (Video 4).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Figure 3a.

claim: Fzd7-ΔPDB expressing cells undergo cell division in arbitrary directions rather than along the mediolateral axis.
source: By co-infecting A coated virus (RCASA) harboring the Fzd7-ΔPDB mutant together with RCASB-H2B-GFP-2A-mCherry into chicken limbs, we achieved super-infection, such that many fluorescently labeled cells became rounder and disorganized (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) undergoing cell division in arbitrary directions rather than along the mediolateral axis (Figure 3a) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) (Video 4).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3a and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Despite misorientation, Fzd7-ΔPDB expressing sister cells remained physically coupled after cytokinesis.
source: Interestingly, despite their misorientation, sister cells remained physically coupled (Figure 3a and b) and underwent pivot behavior (Figure 3c and d) (Video 5).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by data from n=5 cell pairs shown in Figure 3b.

claim: Fzd7-ΔPDB expressing sister cells underwent pivot behavior.
source: Interestingly, despite their misorientation, sister cells remained physically coupled (Figure 3a and b) and underwent pivot behavior (Figure 3c and d) (Video 5).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3c and 3d.

claim: Seven out of 18 Fzd7-ΔPDB expressing cell doublets underwent pivot to form single stacks.
source: Among 18 cell doublets, seven pairs underwent pivot to form single stacks.
evidence: This quantitative result is stated in the figure caption based on analysis shown in Figure 3d.

claim: In tissues with exogenous DVL2-ΔPDZ, sister cells were associated after cytokinesis.
source: In the tissues with exogenous DVL2- ΔPDZ, sister cells were associated after cytokinesis (e, f) (n = 5) and 35% cell doublets were rearranged (g, h) (n = 20).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=5 cell pairs shown in Figure 3e and 3f.

claim: 35% of DVL2-ΔPDZ expressing cell doublets were rearranged.
source: In the tissues with exogenous DVL2- ΔPDZ, sister cells were associated after cytokinesis (e, f) (n = 5) and 35% cell doublets were rearranged (g, h) (n = 20).
evidence: This quantitative result is stated in the figure caption based on n=20 cell doublets shown in Figure 3g and 3h.

claim: In tissues expressing Fzd7, cells did not divide along the mediolateral axis.
source: In the tissues expressing Fzd7 (i, j) or Vangl2 (k, l), cells did not divide along the mediolateral axis (i, k), and were separated within 5 hr after cytokinesis (n = 5 for both cases) (j, l).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption and shown in Figure 3i.

claim: Fzd7 expressing sister cells were separated within 5 hr after cytokinesis.
source: In the tissues expressing Fzd7 (i, j) or Vangl2 (k, l), cells did not divide along the mediolateral axis (i, k), and were separated within 5 hr after cytokinesis (n = 5 for both cases) (j, l).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=5 cell pairs shown in Figure 3j.

claim: No rearrangement was observed between cell doublets in the presence of Fzd7.
source: No rearrangement was observed between cell doublets in the presence of Fzd7 (n = 18) or Vangl2 (n = 16).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=18 cell doublets.

claim: In tissues expressing Vangl2, cells did not divide along the mediolateral axis.
source: In the tissues expressing Fzd7 (i, j) or Vangl2 (k, l), cells did not divide along the mediolateral axis (i, k), and were separated within 5 hr after cytokinesis (n = 5 for both cases) (j, l).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption and shown in Figure 3k.

claim: Vangl2 expressing sister cells were separated within 5 hr after cytokinesis.
source: In the tissues expressing Fzd7 (i, j) or Vangl2 (k, l), cells did not divide along the mediolateral axis (i, k), and were separated within 5 hr after cytokinesis (n = 5 for both cases) (j, l).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=5 cell pairs shown in Figure 3l.

claim: No rearrangement was observed between cell doublets in the presence of Vangl2.
source: No rearrangement was observed between cell doublets in the presence of Fzd7 (n = 18) or Vangl2 (n = 16).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=16 cell doublets.

claim: Cells expressing Fzd7-ΔPDB, Fzd7 or Vangl2 were morphologically more isotropic compared to ellipsoidal wild-type cells.
source: In contrast to the ellipsoidal wild-type cells, the cells expressing Fzd7-ΔPDB, Fzd7 or Vangl2 were morphologically more isotropic.
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure supplement caption and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Wild-type cells were oriented orthogonal to the proximodistal axis, while cells expressing Fzd7-ΔPDB, Fzd7 or Vangl2 exhibited more variations.
source: While wild-type cells were oriented orthogonal to the proximodistal axis, the cells expressing Fzd7-ΔPDB, Fzd7 or Vangl2 exhibited more variations.
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure supplement caption and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Cells expressing Fzd7-ΔPDB showed arbitrary division orientation with significant difference to wild-type cells.
source: Based on the time-lapse images of dividing cells (Figure 3a, (e,I and k), quantitative analysis revealed arbitrary division orientation of the cells expressing Fzd7-ΔPDB (n = 27), Fzd7 (n = 24) and Vangl2 (n = 28) with significant difference to wild-type cells. ** denotes p<0.01 (Watson's U2 test).
evidence: This quantitative result is stated in the figure supplement caption based on n=27 cells shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cells expressing Fzd7 showed arbitrary division orientation with significant difference to wild-type cells.
source: Based on the time-lapse images of dividing cells (Figure 3a, (e,I and k), quantitative analysis revealed arbitrary division orientation of the cells expressing Fzd7-ΔPDB (n = 27), Fzd7 (n = 24) and Vangl2 (n = 28) with significant difference to wild-type cells. ** denotes p<0.01 (Watson's U2 test).
evidence: This quantitative result is stated in the figure supplement caption based on n=24 cells shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cells expressing Vangl2 showed arbitrary division orientation with significant difference to wild-type cells.
source: Based on the time-lapse images of dividing cells (Figure 3a, (e,I and k), quantitative analysis revealed arbitrary division orientation of the cells expressing Fzd7-ΔPDB (n = 27), Fzd7 (n = 24) and Vangl2 (n = 28) with significant difference to wild-type cells. ** denotes p<0.01 (Watson's U2 test).
evidence: This quantitative result is stated in the figure supplement caption based on n=28 cells shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Fzd7-ΔPDB positive clones exhibited either single or complex width.
source: Within each stacked clone, we further measured the SD of θ, the orientation of the topmost cell relative to all the other cells. The results showed that these clones exhibited either single (n = 22) or complex (n = 12) width (c) and they were not parallel to the proximodistal axis (d) (n = 13 and 8 for single and multiple stacks, respectively).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=22 single and n=12 complex clones shown in Figure 4c.

claim: Fzd7-ΔPDB positive clones were not parallel to the proximodistal axis.
source: Within each stacked clone, we further measured the SD of θ, the orientation of the topmost cell relative to all the other cells. The results showed that these clones exhibited either single (n = 22) or complex (n = 12) width (c) and they were not parallel to the proximodistal axis (d) (n = 13 and 8 for single and multiple stacks, respectively).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=13 single and n=8 multiple stacks shown in Figure 4d.

claim: Clonally related cells expressing Fzd7 appeared to be arbitrarily oriented without forming stacks.
source: In the tissues expressing Fzd7-T2A-CFP, Fzd7-T2A-mCherry and Fzd7-T2A-YFP at clonal density, the clonally related cells appeared to be arbitrarily oriented without forming stacks (e).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption and shown in Figure 4e.

claim: The SD of angles between Fzd7 expressing cells and the proximodistal axis was larger than 12°.
source: Consistently, the SD of the angles between these cells to the proximodistal axis (Φ) was larger than 12° (n = 16) (f).
evidence: This quantitative result is stated in the figure caption based on n=16 clones shown in Figure 4f.

claim: With low PCP activity, cells divide in a misoriented manner followed by sister cell association and pivot.
source: With low PCP activity, cells divide in a misoriented manner followed by sister cell association and pivot. In contrast, with enhanced PCP activity, while cells still undergo misoriented divisions, the sister cells become separated and fail to rearrange.
evidence: This model is explicitly stated in the figure caption and illustrated in Figure 4g.

claim: With enhanced PCP activity, cells undergo misoriented divisions and sister cells become separated and fail to rearrange.
source: With low PCP activity, cells divide in a misoriented manner followed by sister cell association and pivot. In contrast, with enhanced PCP activity, while cells still undergo misoriented divisions, the sister cells become separated and fail to rearrange.
evidence: This model is explicitly stated in the figure caption and illustrated in Figure 4g.

claim: Fzd7-YFP was distributed on both the cell membrane and within the cytoplasm.
source: Interestingly, Fzd7-YFP was distributed on both the cell membrane and within the cytoplasm (Figure 5a and f) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) whereas Fzd7-ΔPDB-YFP was largely localized to the cytoplasm (Figure 5b. 5 f).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5a and 5f.

claim: Fzd7-ΔPDB-YFP was largely localized to the cytoplasm.
source: Interestingly, Fzd7-YFP was distributed on both the cell membrane and within the cytoplasm (Figure 5a and f) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) whereas Fzd7-ΔPDB-YFP was largely localized to the cytoplasm (Figure 5b. 5 f).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5b and 5f.

claim: Cell pivot behavior is blocked by excess membrane-bound PCP components.
source: These results suggest that cell pivot behavior is blocked by excess membrane-bound PCP components.
evidence: This interpretation is stated in the text based on the localization data of Fzd7 variants.

claim: Fzd7 was expressed in the cytoplasm and on the membrane.
source: Fzd7 was expressed in the cytoplasm and on the membrane (a) (n = 20), but was constrained to the cytoplasm when lacking its PDB domain (b) (n = 29).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=20 cells shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Fzd7 was constrained to the cytoplasm when lacking its PDB domain.
source: Fzd7 was expressed in the cytoplasm and on the membrane (a) (n = 20), but was constrained to the cytoplasm when lacking its PDB domain (b) (n = 29).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=29 cells shown in Figure 5b.

claim: Removing the VTTE motif from Fzd7 promoted protein cytoplasmic localization.
source: Removing the VTTE motif from and adding it onto Fzd7 promoted protein cytoplasmic and membrane localization, respectively (c, d) (n = 15 and 33 in d and e, respectively).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=15 cells shown in Figure 5c.

claim: Adding the VTTE motif onto Fzd7 promoted protein membrane localization.
source: Removing the VTTE motif from and adding it onto Fzd7 promoted protein cytoplasmic and membrane localization, respectively (c, d) (n = 15 and 33 in d and e, respectively).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=33 cells shown in Figure 5d.

claim: The VTTE truncated mutant was constrained to the cytoplasm.
source: Whereas the KTxxxW truncated version displayed membrane and cytoplasmic distribution similar to that of intact Fzd7 (data not shown), the VTTE truncated mutant was constrained to the cytoplasm (Figure 5c and f), similar to Fzd7-ΔPDB-YFP.
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5c and 5f.

claim: The VTTE motif is critical for membrane localization of Fzd7-YFP.
source: Hence, the VTTE motif is critical for membrane localization of Fzd7-YFP.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the text based on the localization experiments with VTTE mutants.

claim: Adding the VTTE motif onto the C-terminus of Fzd7 promoted membrane binding.
source: Further supporting this, we found that adding the VTTE motif onto the C-terminus of Fzd7 promoted membrane binding (Figure 5d and f) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5d, 5f, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Fzd7-YFP and Fzd7-YFP-VTTE were bound to the membrane.
source: Chick humerus expressing membrane-RFP (red) in combination with either Fzd7-YFP (green) (a) or Fzd7-YFP-VTTE (green) (b) was sectioned and imaged. In both cases, the fusion protein was bound to the membrane.
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure supplement caption and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: N-cadherin was mainly distributed on the membrane with small amounts within the cytoplasm of interphase cells.
source: Immunofluorescence demonstrated that Ncad was mainly distributed on the membrane with small amounts within the cytoplasm of interphase cells; however, it was greatly enriched between closely associated cells (Figure 6a, Romereim et al., 2014).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text with citation to (Romereim et al., 2014) and shown in Figure 6a.

claim: N-cadherin was greatly enriched between closely associated cells.
source: Immunofluorescence demonstrated that Ncad was mainly distributed on the membrane with small amounts within the cytoplasm of interphase cells; however, it was greatly enriched between closely associated cells (Figure 6a, Romereim et al., 2014).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text with citation to (Romereim et al., 2014) and shown in Figure 6a.

claim: N-cadherin was not located in the cleavage furrow but concentrated between closely associated cells at post-cleavage stage.
source: Interestingly, counter-staining of contractile rings demonstrated that this sub-population of Ncad was not located in the cleavage furrow (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), but rather concentrated between closely associated cells that appeared to be at post-cleavage stage.
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Junctional N-cadherin in Fzd7 positive tissues was reduced.
source: However, junctional Ncad in Fzd7 positive tissues was reduced (c). This was confirmed by normalizing junctional Ncad intensity to total Ncad intensity in each pair of sister cells (d) (n = 10, 10, eight for wild-type, Fzd7-ΔPDB, and Fzd7 tissues, respectively).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption and shown in Figure 6c and 6d based on n=8 Fzd7 tissues.

claim: N-cadherin-GFP was enriched in the interface of sister cells in wild-type tissues over time.
source: In the chick metacarpals expressing Ncad-GFP (green) via RCAS infection, live imaging revealed that the fusion protein was enriched in the interface of sister cells in wild-type tissues (e) (n = 6) and tissues coexpressing Fzd7-ΔPDB (n = 6) over time (f).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=6 wild-type tissues shown in Figure 6e.

claim: N-cadherin-GFP was enriched in the interface of sister cells in tissues coexpressing Fzd7-ΔPDB over time.
source: In the chick metacarpals expressing Ncad-GFP (green) via RCAS infection, live imaging revealed that the fusion protein was enriched in the interface of sister cells in wild-type tissues (e) (n = 6) and tissues coexpressing Fzd7-ΔPDB (n = 6) over time (f).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=6 Fzd7-ΔPDB tissues shown in Figure 6f.

claim: In the presence of Fzd7, N-cadherin was initially concentrated in the junctions but then diminished as the cytoplasmic bridge between sister cells disconnected.
source: In contrast, in the presence of Fzd7, Ncad was initially concentrated in the junctions but then diminished as the cytoplasmic bridge between sister cells disconnected (g) (n = 7).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=7 tissues shown in Figure 6g.

claim: N-cadherin-GFP signal in Fzd7 expressing cells dropped about 50% 5 hr after cytokinesis.
source: Changes of cumulative F/Fmax showed that Ncad-GFP signal in Fzd7 expressing cells dropped about 50% 5 hr after cytokinesis.
evidence: This quantitative result is stated in the figure caption and shown in Figure 6h.

claim: Treatment with α-N-cadherin antibody caused sister cells to disengage.
source: Live imaging was performed on H2B-GFP (green) and mCherry (red) positive tissues cultured in the medium with α-Ncad antibody (1:10 dilution) (i), demonstrating the disengagement of sister cells (j) (n = 5).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=5 tissues shown in Figure 6i and 6j.

claim: No complete pivoting was observed in cell doublets treated with α-N-cadherin antibody.
source: In both cases, no complete pivoting was observed in cell doublets (n = 15 and 20 for α-Ncad antibody and dnNcad-T2A-mCherry, respectively).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=15 cell doublets.

claim: Expression of dominant-negative N-cadherin caused similar cell behaviors to α-N-cadherin antibody treatment.
source: Similar cell behaviors were observed in the tissues expressing H2B-GFP (green) and a dominant-negative mutant of Ncad fused to mCherry through T2A sequence (red) (k, l) (n = 5).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=5 tissues shown in Figure 6k and 6l.

claim: No complete pivoting was observed in cell doublets expressing dominant-negative N-cadherin.
source: In both cases, no complete pivoting was observed in cell doublets (n = 15 and 20 for α-Ncad antibody and dnNcad-T2A-mCherry, respectively).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure caption based on n=20 cell doublets.

claim: Functional blocking of N-cadherin causes sister cells to separate.
source: Schematic diagram to show functional blocking of Ncad causes sister cells to separate.
evidence: This model is explicitly stated in the figure caption and illustrated in Figure 6m.

claim: The absolute level of PCP signaling is essential for oriented cell division.
source: Schematic diagram to summarize the roles of PCP signaling and junctional Ncad in regulating single column formation: (1) the absolute level PCP signaling is essential for oriented cell division, (2) PCP signaling reduces Ncad enrichment at the post-cleavage furrow, (3) normal junctional Ncad function is required for cell association and pivot.
evidence: This model is explicitly stated in the figure caption and illustrated in Figure 6n.

claim: PCP signaling reduces N-cadherin enrichment at the post-cleavage furrow.
source: Schematic diagram to summarize the roles of PCP signaling and junctional Ncad in regulating single column formation: (1) the absolute level PCP signaling is essential for oriented cell division, (2) PCP signaling reduces Ncad enrichment at the post-cleavage furrow, (3) normal junctional Ncad function is required for cell association and pivot.
evidence: This model is explicitly stated in the figure caption and illustrated in Figure 6n.

claim: Normal junctional N-cadherin function is required for cell association and pivot.
source: Schematic diagram to summarize the roles of PCP signaling and junctional Ncad in regulating single column formation: (1) the absolute level PCP signaling is essential for oriented cell division, (2) PCP signaling reduces Ncad enrichment at the post-cleavage furrow, (3) normal junctional Ncad function is required for cell association and pivot.
evidence: This model is explicitly stated in the figure caption and illustrated in Figure 6n.

claim: N-cadherin was not strongly expressed in the cleavage furrow.
source: In the cleavage furrow highlighted by actin-rich contractile ring (b1), Ncad was not strongly expressed (b2), whereas this protein was concentrated between the cells with weak junctional phalloidin signal (c, d).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure supplement caption and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1b.

claim: N-cadherin was concentrated between cells with weak junctional phalloidin signal.
source: In the cleavage furrow highlighted by actin-rich contractile ring (b1), Ncad was not strongly expressed (b2), whereas this protein was concentrated between the cells with weak junctional phalloidin signal (c, d).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure supplement caption and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1c and 1d.

claim: The colocalization efficiency between N-cadherin and cleavage furrow was below 0.5.
source: In either case, the colocalization efficiency was below 0.5 (1 represents perfect correlation, 0 represents no correlation, −1 represent perfect anti-correlation). Taken together, it shows this protein is not enriched in the cleavage furrow, but likely in the post-cleavage furrow instead.
evidence: This quantitative result is stated in the figure supplement caption and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1e.

claim: N-cadherin is not enriched in the cleavage furrow, but likely in the post-cleavage furrow instead.
source: In either case, the colocalization efficiency was below 0.5 (1 represents perfect correlation, 0 represents no correlation, −1 represent perfect anti-correlation). Taken together, it shows this protein is not enriched in the cleavage furrow, but likely in the post-cleavage furrow instead.
evidence: This interpretation is stated in the figure supplement caption based on the colocalization analysis.

claim: The expression level of N-cadherin mRNA appeared to be normal in cells expressing Fzd7 or Fzd7-ΔPDB.
source: Double DNA in situ hybridization against Fzd7 (green) and Ncad (red) and was performed in the frozen cartilage sections sparsely expressing either Fzd7 (a) (n = 25) or Fzd7-ΔPDB (b) (n = 23) via low-titer RCAS infection. In both cases, the expression level of Ncad mRNA appeared to be normal when compared with the uninfected chondrocytes within the same context.
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure supplement caption based on n=25 Fzd7 and n=23 Fzd7-ΔPDB expressing cells shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Before cell division, N-cadherin distribution was generally uniform in the cells.
source: Before cell division (T = 0 hr), Ncad distribution was generally uniform in the cells, as demonstrated by the flat profile of the blue lines.
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure supplement caption and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3b-d.

claim: Shortly after division, N-cadherin-GFP was enriched in the junction.
source: Shortly after division (T = 5 hr), Ncad-GFP was enriched in the junction, as suggested by the bell-shaped profile of the red and green lines.
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure supplement caption and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3b-d.

claim: Junctional enrichment of N-cadherin was maintained in wild-type and Fzd7-ΔPDB expressing cartilage at T = 10 hr.
source: Later on (T = 10 hr), while junctional enrichment of Ncad was still maintained in wild-type (b) and Fzd7-ΔPDB (c) expressing cartilage, it vanished in Fzd7 expressing tissues (d).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure supplement caption and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3b and 3c.

claim: Junctional enrichment of N-cadherin vanished in Fzd7 expressing tissues at T = 10 hr.
source: Later on (T = 10 hr), while junctional enrichment of Ncad was still maintained in wild-type (b) and Fzd7-ΔPDB (c) expressing cartilage, it vanished in Fzd7 expressing tissues (d).
evidence: This observation is stated in the figure supplement caption and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3d.

claim: 80% of partial intercalation occurred within the same multi-column clone.
source: Although this time period is not sufficient to follow complete intercalation, we observed partial intercalation within the same multi-column clone (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a) (Video 15) (80%), as well as some examples of intercalation between non-clonally related cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2b) (Video 16) (20%).
evidence: This quantitative result is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 2a.

claim: 20% of partial intercalation occurred between non-clonally related cells.
source: Although this time period is not sufficient to follow complete intercalation, we observed partial intercalation within the same multi-column clone (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a) (Video 15) (80%), as well as some examples of intercalation between non-clonally related cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2b) (Video 16) (20%).
evidence: This quantitative result is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 2b.

claim: Both oriented cell divisions and cell rearrangements are critical for proper embryogenesis and organogenesis.
source: Both oriented cell divisions and cell rearrangements are critical for proper embryogenesis and organogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the Abstract as a general principle.

claim: Single chondrocyte precursors can generate both single-column and multi-column clones through oriented division followed by cell rearrangements.
source: By combining retroviral-based multicolor clonal analysis with live imaging, the results show that single chondrocyte precursors can generate both single-column and multi-column clones through oriented division followed by cell rearrangements.
evidence: This is stated in the Abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: After mediolateral cell division, N-cadherin is enriched in the post-cleavage furrow.
source: After mediolateral cell division, N-cadherin is enriched in the post-cleavage furrow; then one cell pivots around the other, resulting in stacking into a column.
evidence: This is stated in the Abstract as a key finding.

claim: After mediolateral cell division, one cell pivots around the other, resulting in stacking into a column.
source: After mediolateral cell division, N-cadherin is enriched in the post-cleavage furrow; then one cell pivots around the other, resulting in stacking into a column.
evidence: This is stated in the Abstract as a key finding.

claim: Planar cell polarity signaling enables cells to pivot in the direction of limb elongation via N-cadherin-mediated coupling.
source: Perturbation analyses demonstrate that planar cell polarity signaling enables cells to pivot in the direction of limb elongation via this N-cadherin-mediated coupling.
evidence: This is stated in the Abstract as a main conclusion.

claim: Oriented cell divisions can drive body axis elongation, as seen in zebrafish gastrulation.
source: By orienting the axis of division in a stereotypic direction, oriented cell divisions serve two major purposes: first they can drive body axis elongation, as seen in zebrafish gastrulation (Gong et al., 2004); second, they can generate cellular diversity, for example by asymmetrically segregating cell fate determinants to produce one stem cell and one differentiated cell, as observed during Drosophila spermatogenesis (Yamashita et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to (Gong et al., 2004).

claim: Oriented cell divisions can generate cellular diversity by asymmetrically segregating cell fate determinants, as observed during Drosophila spermatogenesis.
source: By orienting the axis of division in a stereotypic direction, oriented cell divisions serve two major purposes: first they can drive body axis elongation, as seen in zebrafish gastrulation (Gong et al., 2004); second, they can generate cellular diversity, for example by asymmetrically segregating cell fate determinants to produce one stem cell and one differentiated cell, as observed during Drosophila spermatogenesis (Yamashita et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to (Yamashita et al., 2003).

claim: Cell rearrangements can occur via junctional remodeling whereby adherens junctions between cells shrink in one direction and extend in the orthogonal direction, as seen in Drosophila epithelia tissues.
source: One scenario involves junctional remodeling whereby adherens junctions between cells shrink in one direction and extend in the orthogonal direction, as seen in Drosophila epithelia tissues (Bertet et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to (Bertet et al., 2004).

claim: Cell rearrangements can occur by mediolateral cell intercalation, as exemplified by notochord cells during Xenopus gastrulation.
source: A second example is by mediolateral cell intercalation, as exemplified by notochord cells during Xenopus gastrulation (Wallingford et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to (Wallingford et al., 2000).

claim: Both oriented divisions and cell rearrangements can establish and maintain polarized cell organization that subsequently drives body axis elongation.
source: Both oriented divisions and cell rearrangements can establish and maintain polarized cell organization that subsequently drives body axis elongation (Gillies and Cabernard, 2011; Lau et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to (Gillies and Cabernard, 2011; Lau et al., 2015).

claim: Studies of cellular rearrangement have primarily focused on either slowly dividing or postmitotic cells.
source: For technical reasons, studies of cellular rearrangement have primarily focused on either slowly dividing or postmitotic cells (Gillies and Cabernard, 2011; Lau et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to (Gillies and Cabernard, 2011; Lau et al., 2015).

claim: Along the proximodistal axis of growth plate cartilage, chondrocytes undergo progressive maturation and collagen deposition.
source: Along the proximodistal axis of the tissue, chondrocytes undergo progressive maturation and collagen deposition; once terminally differentiated, hypertrophic chondrocytes are replaced by osteoblasts that lay down a calcified matrix to form long bones (Figure 1a) (Kronenberg, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to (Kronenberg, 2003) and illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: Once terminally differentiated, hypertrophic chondrocytes are replaced by osteoblasts that lay down a calcified matrix to form long bones.
source: Along the proximodistal axis of the tissue, chondrocytes undergo progressive maturation and collagen deposition; once terminally differentiated, hypertrophic chondrocytes are replaced by osteoblasts that lay down a calcified matrix to form long bones (Figure 1a) (Kronenberg, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to (Kronenberg, 2003) and illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: The directional growth of proliferative chondrocytes is critical for normal cartilage homeostasis, morphogenesis and regeneration.
source: The directional growth of proliferative chondrocytes is critical for normal cartilage homeostasis, morphogenesis and regeneration (Dodds, 1930; Li and Dudley, 2009; Le Pabic et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to (Dodds, 1930; Li and Dudley, 2009; Le Pabic et al., 2014).

claim: Developing chondrocytes acquire an ellipsoidal shape and orient mitotic figures orthogonal to the tissue proximodistal axis.
source: Developing chondrocytes have several hallmark features: they acquire an ellipsoidal shape and orient mitotic figures orthogonal to the tissue proximodistal (PD) axis; clonally related cells are thought to be arranged in columns along the PD axis (Dodds, 1930; Li and Dudley, 2009; Le Pabic et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to (Dodds, 1930; Li and Dudley, 2009; Le Pabic et al., 2014).

claim: Clonally related chondrocytes are thought to be arranged in columns along the proximodistal axis.
source: Developing chondrocytes have several hallmark features: they acquire an ellipsoidal shape and orient mitotic figures orthogonal to the tissue proximodistal (PD) axis; clonally related cells are thought to be arranged in columns along the PD axis (Dodds, 1930; Li and Dudley, 2009; Le Pabic et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to (Dodds, 1930; Li and Dudley, 2009; Le Pabic et al., 2014).

claim: It has been proposed that chondrocyte column formation is comprised of sequential steps of oriented division and subsequent cell rearrangement.
source: Based on these observations, it has been proposed that chondrocyte column formation is comprised of sequential steps of oriented division and subsequent cell rearrangement (Figure 1b) (Dodds, 1930).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to (Dodds, 1930) and illustrated in Figure 1b.

claim: Some studies suggest that chondrocyte columns may be more complex, with two to three adjacent stacks.
source: Although this simple model predicts that clonally related cells form a single column, some studies suggest that columns may be more complex, with two to three adjacent stacks (Li and Dudley, 2009; Ahrens et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to (Li and Dudley, 2009; Ahrens et al., 2009).

claim: Columnar structure cannot be visualized histologically in embryonic growth plate cartilage.
source: Further complicating the analysis of the embryonic growth plate cartilage, columnar structure cannot be visualized histologically (Li and Dudley, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to (Li and Dudley, 2009).

claim: Planar cell polarity signaling has been suggested in coordinating oriented division and column formation in developing growth plate cartilage.
source: Planar cell polarity (PCP) signaling previously has been suggested in coordinating oriented division and column formation in developing growth plate cartilage (Li and Dudley, 2009; Le Pabic et al., 2014; Gao et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to (Li and Dudley, 2009; Le Pabic et al., 2014; Gao et al., 2011).

claim: The majority of proliferating cartilage clones displayed monocolor, suggesting each cluster represents a clone.
source: The results showed that limb cartilage was comprised of clustered cells with the majority displaying monocolor (Figure 1d and f), strongly suggesting that each cluster represents a clone.
evidence: This observation is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1d and 1f.

claim: All single column clones were monoclonal.
source: Whereas all the single column clones (the red clone, Figure 1f1) and most multi-column clones (92%) (the blue and green clones, Figure 1f2) were monoclonal, a minority of multi-column clones (8%) intermixed with non-clonally related cells (white arrow pointing to the uninfected cell beside the green clone, Figure 1f1).
evidence: This observation is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1f1.

claim: 92% of multi-column clones were monoclonal.
source: Whereas all the single column clones (the red clone, Figure 1f1) and most multi-column clones (92%) (the blue and green clones, Figure 1f2) were monoclonal, a minority of multi-column clones (8%) intermixed with non-clonally related cells (white arrow pointing to the uninfected cell beside the green clone, Figure 1f1).
evidence: This quantitative result is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1f2.

claim: 8% of multi-column clones intermixed with non-clonally related cells.
source: Whereas all the single column clones (the red clone, Figure 1f1) and most multi-column clones (92%) (the blue and green clones, Figure 1f2) were monoclonal, a minority of multi-column clones (8%) intermixed with non-clonally related cells (white arrow pointing to the uninfected cell beside the green clone, Figure 1f1).
evidence: This quantitative result is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1f1.

claim: Proliferating cartilage is a mosaic of simple and multi-column monoclones, with a minor contribution resulting from intermixing between neighboring clones.
source: Thus, proliferating cartilage is a mosaic of simple and multi-column monoclones, with a minor contribution resulting from intermixing between neighboring clones,
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Results section based on the clonal analysis data.

claim: Oriented division is sensitive to both high and low PCP activity.
source: Together with the loss-of-function studies, these results show that oriented division is sensitive to both high and low PCP activity, whereas cell pivot behavior is only inhibited by high PCP activity (Figure 4g).
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Results section based on the perturbation experiments and illustrated in Figure 4g.

claim: Cell pivot behavior is only inhibited by high PCP activity.
source: Together with the loss-of-function studies, these results show that oriented division is sensitive to both high and low PCP activity, whereas cell pivot behavior is only inhibited by high PCP activity (Figure 4g).
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Results section based on the perturbation experiments and illustrated in Figure 4g.

claim: Oriented division and cell pivot behavior are coupled but respond differently to the level of PCP signaling.
source: Hence, these two cellular events are coupled but respond differently to the level of PCP signaling.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Results section based on the differential responses to PCP perturbation.

claim: In epithelia cells, the PDB domain is essential for the subcellular localization and signaling specificity of Fzd.
source: In epithelia cells, this domain is essential for the subcellular localization and signaling specificity of Fzd (Wu et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation to (Wu et al., 2004).

claim: PCP proteins have been shown to promote internalization of cadherins from the membrane and adherens junctions in epithelial cells.
source: PCP proteins have been shown to promote internalization of cadherins from the membrane and adherens junctions in epithelial cells (Warrington et al., 2013; Nagaoka et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to (Warrington et al., 2013; Nagaoka et al., 2014).

claim: Cadherins are important to normal limb chondrogenesis and craniofacial skeletal growth.
source: Additionally, cadherins are important to normal limb chondrogenesis and craniofacial skeletal growth (Oberlender and Tuan, 1994; Romereim et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to (Oberlender and Tuan, 1994; Romereim et al., 2014).

claim: In growth plate cartilage, excess membrane-bound Fzd might prevent cell pivoting by reducing local cadherin concentration.
source: Hence, we hypothesized that in growth plate cartilage, excess membrane-bound Fzd might prevent cell pivoting by reducing local cadherin concentration.
evidence: This hypothesis is stated in the Results section based on the observations of Fzd and cadherin interactions.

claim: N-cadherin transcript levels appeared normal in tissues expressing either Fzd7 or Fzd7-ΔPDB.
source: In the tissues expressing either Fzd7 or Fzd7-ΔPDB, Ncad transcript levels appeared normal (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This observation is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Immunofluorescence analysis failed to detect obvious differences in the amount of membrane and cytoplasmic-bound N-cadherin protein in Fzd7 or Fzd7-ΔPDB expressing tissues compared with wild-type tissues.
source: Furthermore, immunofluorescence analysis failed to detect obvious differences in the amount of membrane and cytoplasmic-bound Ncad protein when compared with wild-type tissues (Figure 6a–c).
evidence: This observation is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6a-c.

claim: Junctional N-cadherin was normal in Fzd7-ΔPDB expressing tissues.
source: In contrast, junctional Ncad was diminished in the Fzd7 expressing tissues (Figure 6c and d), while normal in Fzd7-ΔPDB expressing tissues (Figure 6b and d), consistent with the phenotypes observed after PCP and Ncad perturbation studies.
evidence: This observation is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6b and 6d.

claim: PCP signaling inhibits sister cell association and their pivoting via down-regulation of junctional cadherin.
source: Collectively, our results suggest that PCP signaling inhibits sister cell association and their pivoting via down-regulation of junctional cadherin.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Results section based on the N-cadherin dynamics experiments.

claim: Sister chondrocyte cells fail to reorganize into single columns if they do not attach to each other, regardless of their orientation during cell division.
source: In summary, we demonstrate that sister chondrocyte cells, regardless of their orientation during cell division, fail to reorganize into single columns if they do not attach to each other.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Results section based on the experimental findings.

claim: The division orientation is not sufficient to initiate cell pivot behavior; rather, cell association mediated by N-cadherin is critical for their subsequent rearrangement.
source: Although both oriented division and cell rearrangement occur sequentially and are controlled by PCP signaling, the division orientation is not sufficient to initiate cell pivot behavior; rather, cell association mediated by Ncad is critical for their subsequent rearrangement.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Results section based on the experimental findings.

claim: The occurrence of cell pivot is enabled by cell-cell adhesion downstream of PCP signaling whereas the orientation of the cell pivot is determined by the orientation of preceding division.
source: Taken together, we propose that the occurrence of cell pivot is enabled by cell-cell adhesion downstream of PCP signaling whereas the orientation of the cell pivot is determined by the orientation of preceding division (Figure 6n).
evidence: This model is explicitly stated in the Results section and illustrated in Figure 6n.

claim: Chondrocyte cell intercalation is a slow process taking more than 48 hr to reach completion.
source: Previous dynamic imaging using two-photon microscopy showed that chondrocyte cell intercalation is a slow process taking more than 48 hr to reach completion (Li et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation to (Li et al., 2015).

claim: The existence of both cell intercalation and cell pivoting within clones suggests that chondrocytes employ multiple strategies to establish proper tissue architecture.
source: This existence of both cell intercalation and cell pivoting within clones (Figure 2h) suggests that chondrocytes employ multiple strategies to establish proper tissue architecture.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Results section based on the observation of multiple cell behaviors.

claim: Cell pivoting contributes to normal morphogenesis of growth plate cartilage.
source: By combining live imaging and quantitative analyses in chick embryo, we demonstrate that cell pivoting contributes to normal morphogenesis of growth plate cartilage and further confirm the occurrence of mediolateral intercalation within the same context.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental findings.

claim: Mediolateral intercalation occurs within growth plate cartilage.
source: By combining live imaging and quantitative analyses in chick embryo, we demonstrate that cell pivoting contributes to normal morphogenesis of growth plate cartilage and further confirm the occurrence of mediolateral intercalation within the same context.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental findings.

claim: The similarities in chondrocyte behavior in the developing craniofacial and limb skeletal elements suggest that conserved cellular principles are employed to build cylindrical-shaped skeletons during evolution.
source: The similarities in chondrocyte behavior in the developing craniofacial (neural crest-derived) and limb (mesoderm-derived) skeletal elements suggest that, during evolution, conserved cellular principles are employed to build cylindrical-shaped skeletons, even though these tissues are derived from different types of progenitor cells.
evidence: This interpretation is stated in the Discussion section based on comparative observations.

claim: PCP signaling differentially influences distinct steps, regulating the orientation of cell division and enabling cells to pivot by controlling N-cadherin enrichment in the post-cleavage furrow.
source: By delving into the molecular mechanisms underlying cell pivot behavior, we demonstrate that PCP signaling differentially influences distinct steps, regulating the orientation of cell division and enabling cells to pivot by controlling Ncad enrichment in the post-cleavage furrow.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental findings.

claim: Chondrocytes divide along the tissue mediolateral axis due to geometrical constraints.
source: By this means, chondrocytes divide along the tissue mediolateral axis (cell major axis) due to geometrical constraints (Li and Dudley, 2009) while the resultant clones expand mainly in the direction of tissue growth.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation to (Li and Dudley, 2009).

claim: Proliferative chondrocytes are normally embedded in Collagen 2a and cells become disorganized in its mutant mice.
source: Given that proliferative chondrocytes normally are embedded in Collagen 2a and that cells become disorganized in its mutant mice (Barbieri et al., 2003), an intriguing possibility is that the extracellular matrix provides such a constraint.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation to (Barbieri et al., 2003).

claim: The extracellular matrix may provide geometrical constraints for chondrocyte division.
source: Given that proliferative chondrocytes normally are embedded in Collagen 2a and that cells become disorganized in its mutant mice (Barbieri et al., 2003), an intriguing possibility is that the extracellular matrix provides such a constraint.
evidence: This speculation is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Multicolor replication incompetent retroviruses enrich the toolkit for cell lineage analysis in amniotes.
source: By devising multicolor replication incompetent retroviruses for clonal analysis of chondrocytes, our work enriches the toolkit for cell lineage analysis in amniotes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a methodological contribution.

claim: RIA virus offers better levels of infection in many chick tissues such as retina and limb, muscle, skin and feather compared with Confetti techniques mediated by lentiviral delivery.
source: Compared with Confetti techniques mediated by lentiviral delivery (Loulier et al., 2014), the RIA virus offers better levels of infection in many chick tissues such as retina and limb (Pearse et al., 2007), muscle (Gordon et al., 2009), skin and feather (Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This comparison is stated in the Discussion section with citations to multiple studies.

claim: Clonally related chondrocytes become arranged in either single or multi-columns along the axis of tissue elongation.
source: Our results show that clonally related chondrocytes become arranged in either single or multi-columns along the axis of tissue elongation.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Discussion section summarizing the main findings.

claim: The PCP pathway coordinates cell pivoting following mediolateral division.
source: The PCP pathway coordinates cell pivoting following mediolateral division.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Discussion section summarizing the main findings.

claim: Chondrocytes increase their cell numbers while concomitantly undergoing stereotypical arrangements that result in tissue elongation.
source: In this way, chondrocytes increase their cell numbers while concomitantly undergoing stereotypical arrangements that result in tissue elongation.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Discussion section summarizing the main findings.

claim: PCP signaling is important in shaping tissues via regulating polarized cell behaviors.
source: Together with the known roles of PCP signaling in determining the morphology of other tissues and organs (Zallen, 2007), this highlights the importance of PCP signaling in shaping tissues via regulating polarized cell behaviors.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Discussion section with citation to (Zallen, 2007).
